desc: Punk rock is a simplistic and aggressive style of rock music which usually features an anti-establishment ethos. Punk has numerous subgenres, including hardcore punk (which is more abrasive, more aggressive, and is known for having short songs), d-beat (hardcore influenced by metal), and crust punk--all of which have influenced metal, been influenced by metal, or both, all to varying degrees. For almost as long as they've existed, punk and metal have had a mutually derivative relationship.

Heavy metal is both a subgenre and the umbrella that every other metal genre falls under. The term was coined to describe all metal music, but as more subgenres have developed, the term has been applied retroactively to all music that is in the same style as that first wave of metal bands. Heavy metal is an outgrowth of hard rock that features the same power chord riffs, but is heavier, faster, and usually focuses on darker subject matter. Notable heavy metal acts include Black Sabbath, Rainbow, Dio, Deep Purple, and Mercyful Fate.

This particularly atmospheric subgenre is considered the oldest metal subgenre, as it can be traced back directly to Black Sabbath, who is widely considered to be the first heavy metal band as well as the first doom metal band. Doom Metal features slow tempos, thick guitar distortion, and an ominous or dreadful atmosphere. Doom Metal songs also tend to be quite long, frequently reaching 10 minutes or more. Some notable Doom Metal bands are Black Sabbath, Pentagram, Saint Vitus, Trouble, Candlemass, and Witchfinder General.

'NWOBHM' stands for 'New Wave of British Heavy Metal.' NWOBHM is associated less with a particular sound than with a particular time, place, and set of bands. It essentially just describes those British heavy metal bands that sprung up as the popularity of bands like Black Sabbath started to wane. Notable NWOBHM bands include Iron Maiden, Saxon, Venom, Witchfinder General, and Def Leppard.

Speed Metal is harder to define; it shares a lot of similiarities with heavy metal and NWOBHM, and it was also short lived and quickly overtaken by thrash metal. Speed Metal is heavy metal that is--you guessed it--faster and more aggressive. Some Speed Metal acts also vie for a rawer, more punk-like sound (e.g. bands like Venom). Motorhead is perhaps the most agreed upon example of Speed Metal, but bands like Venom, Running Wild, Exciter, and Enforcer are also considered Speed Metal. While Speed Metal was short-lived, it has found new life in modern bands like Hellripper and Bewitcher.

First wave black metal is a looser term used to describe a handful of heavy/speed/thrash metal bands that were particularly dark or raw sounding and that influenced the Norwegian black metal scene of the 1990s (and this scene is what established the standard black metal sound). The reign of the first wave of black metal was a time in which genres weren't so clearly defined, so a lot of thrash metal bands' early work was also considered black metal at the time. Notable 1st wave black metal bands include Venom, Bathory, Hellhammer, Celtic Frost, Mercyful Fate, early Sodom/Kreator/Desctruction/Slayer/Sepultura, Sacrofago, and Blasphemy. The genre takes its name from Venom's second album, titled 'Black Metal.'

In the early 80s, many bands were inspired by punk bands like Discharge as well as NWOBHM/speed bands like Motorhead and Venom, and developed a fast, aggressive style of heavy metal dubbed 'thrash metal.' Thrash metal is known for its speed and aggression, featuring fast, double bass drumming and palm muted / technical riffs/solos. The vocals of thrash can vary quite a bit, with some bands like Artillery embracing the same melodic style of bands before (e.g. Iron Maiden) while bands like Slayer or Sodom shouting or almost-growling. Notable thrash bands include Metallica, Megadeth, Anthrax, Slayer, Kreator, Sodom, Destruction, Tankard, Sepultura, Overkill, Exodus, Nuclear Assault, Void, and honestly many more. It's also worth noting the existence of 'crossover thrash,' (the 'crossover' being between punk and thrash metal) which developed in the US East Coast thrash metal scene, where thrash bands took notably more inspiration from punk.

Black Metal found its footing in Norway in the early 90s. A handful of bands from the country took inspiration from first wave bands like Venom, Bathory, Celtic Frost, Mercyful fate, etc and developed their own sound: trebly, lo-fi tremolo-picked riffs with double bass drumming (and/or blast beats) and shrieking vocals. Black metal lyrics/imagery usually focuses on darkness, satanism, paganism, and the occult. Notable black metal bands include Darkthrone, Emperor, Immortal, Burzum, Mayhem, and Gorgoroth.

Death Metal is easy to think of as having a direct link to thrash metal. Many of the first death metal bands took significant inspiration from thrash metal bands, or they were thrash metal bands themselves (e.g. Possessed). Death metal features the same fast tempos, double bass drumming, and palm muting (and in many cases technicality) of thrash metal, but the guitars are downtuned, given more distortion, and the singing/shouting has been replaced with straight up growling (known by many as 'death growls'). Death metal usually covers subject matter like death (shocker), disease, gore/horror, and satanism. Some significant death metal bands are Possessed, Death, Obituary, Deicide, Morbid Angel, Pestilence, Autopsy, Bolt Thrower, Carcass, Cannibal Corpse, Incantation, Suffocation, Immolation, Dismember, Entombed, Gorguts, Cryptopsy, and many more.

Grindcore is a fusion between 'extreme metal,' (in other words, the umbrella that houses subgenres like death metal and thrash metal) and hardcore punk. Grindcore is extremely fast, known for its 'blast beats' and extremely short songs (as short as four seconds!). Vocals tend to be shrieking or growling. Notable grindcore bands include Napalm Death, Terrorizer, Repulsion, Pig Destroyer, Nuclear Death, Insect Warfare, Carcass, and Anal Cunt.
